units.source_text: “见我只知道买书，夫人就说，你也该置办些衣物。

en.t: Seeing that I did nothing but buy books, the lady of the house said, "You ought to get yourself some clothes too."

units.source_text: 实际上，我也只有乡下人织的棉布衣裳，那时候的学生还不穿绸布衣服。

en.t: In fact, all I had were cotton clothes woven by country people; students in those days did not yet wear silk garments.

units.source_text: 有个同学家好像是在横滨经商的，家里生活很铺张。

en.t: One of my classmates seemed to come from a family doing business in Yokohama, and they lived rather lavishly.

units.source_text: 有一次家里给他寄来一件纯白纺绸小袄，大家见了，都笑了起来。

en.t: Once his family sent him a pure white habutae silk padded jacket, and when everyone saw it, they all burst out laughing.

units.source_text: 同学觉得很不好意思，一味辩解，还把家里专门给他寄来的这件小袄塞进行李底下，不再穿了。

en.t: The classmate felt terribly embarrassed and kept making excuses, then stuffed the jacket his family had especially sent him into the bottom of his trunk and never wore it again.

units.source_text: 可是，大家伙又起哄，非要他穿不可，没想到拿出来一看，那件小袄上竟爬满了虱子。

en.t: But the others started teasing him again and insisted that he wear it; when he took it out, to everyone's surprise the jacket was crawling with lice.

units.source_text: 那个同学大概是觉得有了合适的借口吧，把这件遭人取笑的小袄卷成一团，一起出去散步时，顺便扔进了根津的脏水沟里。

en.t: That classmate probably felt he now had a good excuse, so he rolled up the much-ridiculed jacket and, while we were out for a walk together, tossed it into a filthy ditch in Nezu.

units.source_text: 我站在桥上，笑嘻嘻地看着他扔小袄，心里丝毫没有感到可惜。

en.t: I stood on the bridge, grinning as I watched him throw the jacket away, and did not feel the slightest regret.
